name: buzz
one_liner: A private chat-and-workspace tool where humans and AI agents work together on a server you control, instead of inside a third-party cloud SaaS.
buyer: A small engineering team or open-source maintainer who wants humans and AI agents collaborating in one place without their conversations and data sitting on someone else's servers.
business_use_cases: A dev team self-hosts it as an internal 'agent ops center' where multiple AI agents post updates and humans direct them, replacing ad hoc chat bots.
An open-source project runs a public instance so contributors and maintainer bots coordinate issues and PRs transparently.
A privacy-sensitive company, such as a law or healthcare firm, adopts it instead of a cloud chat tool specifically because agent conversations never leave its own infrastructure.

money_ideas.idea: Offer paid managed hosting with backups and SSO for teams that like the product but don't want to run the server themselves
Sell a 'bring your own agents' integration package to companies rolling out AI agents at work who need help wiring them into it

steal_this: This is early, visionary infrastructure rather than a finished product — the realistic weekend move is becoming the easiest managed-hosting provider for it before anyone else does, not building a feature on top yet.
